Adds every contact in the selection who is not on a list yet: `pending` on a double-opt-in
list, `subscribed` otherwise. An existing membership is left exactly as it is: `pending` is not

This deliberately differs from `POST /lists/{id}/members`, which lets an unsubscribed contact
back in. One admin re-adding one named person is a considered act they answer for; a bulk
action over thousands involves no per-person judgement, and reviving opt-outs en masse is what
gets a sender blocklisted. Do not "fix" the asymmetry.

display_name.description: Used only when this accept creates the account.

password.description: Required, 12 to 256 characters, when no account exists for the invited address.

ApiKeySummary.description: A key as listed: its prefix identifies it, nothing in it can authenticate.

note.description: States, so no client has to guess, that deleting did not delete data.

AuditEntry.description:
One audit row, as stored. `metadata` is returned verbatim, which is why writers must never put
a secret in it.

`actor_email` and `actor_api_key_prefix` name the actor the ids point at, resolved by the two
LEFT JOINs in `list`. They are a convenience for display, not a second identity: the ids stay
authoritative, and either name is `None` once the user or key behind it has been deleted —
`audit_log` has no foreign keys on purpose, so its rows outlive both.

actor_api_key_prefix.description: The key's public prefix, without the `nm_` scheme: a key is shown as `nm_{prefix}`.

Block.description:
The standing block that stops one address being mailed, and nothing else about it: not the
row's id, note or who made it, and never another address.

scope.description: Whether it blocks this one address or every address on its domain.

BlockLevel.description: Whose block it is: this workspace's own, or one set instance-wide that every workspace inherits.

BulkResult.description:
What a bulk action did, as two numbers taken from the same statement. `affected` is how many
contacts it changed; `selected` is how many the selection matched (as of its `as_of`, less the
exclusions). `affected` is lower whenever some were already in the wanted state, so the UI can
say "N of M".

oneOf.description:
Only for `subscribe`: the status the new memberships were written with. `pending` means
the contacts are on a double-opt-in list and not mailable until they confirm, and nothing
in this milestone confirms them: `affected` is not a count of people who can be mailed.

BulkTarget.description: What a bulk route acts on: exactly one of a filter selection or an explicit list of contacts.

excluded_ids.description: Contacts to leave out of a `selection_token`. At most 10 000.

ids.description:
These contacts and no others, e.g. the ticked rows of a table: at most 10 000. Ids that are
not in this workspace select nothing. Cannot be combined with `excluded_ids`.

selection_token.description:
From `POST /contacts/selection`: every contact its filter matched, as of then, less
`excluded_ids`. Send this or `ids`, not both and not neither.

challenge_id.description: Send back with the browser's answer.

options.description: The WebAuthn `publicKey` options object, as `@simplewebauthn/browser` expects.

attributes.description: Custom field values by field key. Values of archived fields stay readable here.

ContactFilter.description:
Which contacts a list shows. It is embedded in a signed selection token later, so its
serialised form is part of that token's payload: renaming a field, or adding one (the payload is
not tolerant of a missing field), would make tokens already issued fail to decode, as a
`422 selection-invalid`, until they age out after an hour. Mind that during a rolling deploy.

list_id.description:
Contacts with a membership row on this list, whatever its status: a `pending` or
`unsubscribed` member is still a member here. A list of another workspace matches nothing.

oneOf.description:
Narrows `list_id` to the memberships with this status. Meaningless without `list_id`: the
handler refuses it, and `list` ignores it.

q.description: Case-insensitive substring of the address or name.

tag_id.description: Contacts with this tag. A tag of another workspace matches nothing.

ContactList.description: One list a contact is on, as the contact's page shows it.

ContactSort.description:
What a contact list is ordered by. Only keys with an index (`contacts_keyset_created`,
`contacts_keyset_email`) are offered: a sort by name would sort the whole workspace per page.

CreatedApiKey.description: The one response that carries the key.

CreatedInvite.description: The one response that carries the token, inside `invite_url`.

archived_at.description: Set when the field was deleted. Contacts keep their values until the field is purged.

options.description: The allowed values of a `select` or `multi_select` field; empty for every other kind.

Eligibility.description: Whether a contact may be mailed, and if a standing block stops it, which one.

oneOf.description:
The block that stops this address, whether it is this workspace's or the whole instance's.
It says nothing about any other address. A list membership that is `pending` or
`unsubscribed` is a separate reason a contact is not mailed on that list, and is not here.

FieldKind.description: How a field's value is typed, stored as snake_case text (a `check` constraint, not an enum).

credential.description: The browser's `PublicKeyCredential`, in WebAuthn JSON form.

InvitePreview.description: What the invitee sees before accepting.

account_exists.description: Whether to show a sign-in or a set-a-password form.

InviteSummary.description: An open invite as the workspace's admins see it: no token, no URL.

double_optin.description:
`true`: a new member is `pending` until they confirm. `false`: a new member is
`subscribed` at once.

visibility.description: Unused until the preference center, which shows the `public` lists as topics.

ListMember.description: A contact's standing on one list.

subscribed_at.description: Null while `pending`, and after an unsubscribe is undone on a double-opt-in list.

unsubscribed_at.description: Set only while the status is `unsubscribed`.

methods.description: The second factors on offer; present only for `mfa_required`.

status.description:
`ok` once signed in; `mfa_required` when a second factor must follow at
`POST /api/v1/auth/login/totp` (the cookie set is then a 10-minute pending session).

MembershipStatus.description:
What a membership row says. It means the same on every list: `Pending` is written only on a
double-opt-in list, `Subscribed` is written at once on a single-opt-in one, and nothing here
depends on the list's setting. A `Pending` row can outlive the list's
double opt-in being switched off: it still means "not confirmed" and is not mailable.

role.description: `viewer`, `editor` or `admin`, and no higher than the caller's own role.

NewContact.description: A contact to insert. Nothing here is trusted: `create` validates every field.

attributes.description: Custom field values by field key; see `validate_attributes` for what each kind accepts.

email.description: Normalised (trimmed, NFC, lowercased) before it is stored.

timezone.description: An IANA time zone such as `Europe/London`.

key.description:
`^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,62}$`. The JSONB key every contact's value is stored under; it cannot
change afterwards.

options.description: Required (1-200 distinct values) for `select` and `multi_select`; omit for every other kind.

NewSuppression.description:
A suppression to add. `scope` decides which of `email` and `domain` is required, and the other
must be absent.

domain.description: Required for `domain`, such as `spam.example`. Matches that exact domain only: subdomains are NOT covered (`spam.example` leaves `mail.spam.example` mailable).

email.description: Required for `address`. Normalised (trimmed, NFC, lowercased) before it is stored.

note.description: Up to 500 characters; line breaks are allowed.

reason.description: Anything but `gdpr_erasure`, which only erasing a contact writes.

timezone.description: An IANA zone such as `Europe/London`; defaults to `UTC`.

items.description: A key as listed: its prefix identifies it, nothing in it can authenticate.

options.description: The allowed values of a `select` or `multi_select` field; empty for every other kind.

items.description: An open invite as the workspace's admins see it: no token, no URL.

double_optin.description:
`true`: a new member is `pending` until they confirm. `false`: a new member is
`subscribed` at once.

visibility.description: Unused until the preference center, which shows the `public` lists as topics.

items.description: A contact's standing on one list.

subscribed_at.description: Null while `pending`, and after an unsubscribe is undone on a double-opt-in list.

unsubscribed_at.description: Set only while the status is `unsubscribed`.

items.description: A passkey as listed: nothing in it can authenticate.
A suppression as the API shows it. There is deliberately no hash field here.

email.description: Address scope only; null on an erasure tombstone, whose plaintext was destroyed.

lifted_at.description: Set when lifted. A lifted row stays, as history.

workspace_id.description: Null for an instance-wide suppression, which applies to every workspace.

items.description: A workspace as one caller sees it: `role` is the caller's own.

PasskeySummary.description: A passkey as listed: nothing in it can authenticate.

affected.description: Contacts whose value for the field was removed.

Reason.description: Why an address is blocked. Stored as text under a `check` constraint, not a Postgres enum.

Role.description:
A member's role, stored as lowercase text. Variants run from least to most privileged:
`authorize` compares roles with `<`, so the order here is load-bearing.

SelectionToken.description: The signed token for a selection; see `selection`.

selected.description:
How many contacts the filter matches, as of the token's `as_of`. A live count over the
whole match: deliberately exempt from the 150 ms p95 target, like
`GET /lists/{id}/mailable-count`, because counting ten million rows is slow. The UI asks
for it when the user asks to select everything, and shows a skeleton until it lands. It is
never kept as a counter on a table: hand-maintained counters drift.

selection_token.description: Valid for one hour. Pass it to a `bulk/*` route.

Suppression.description: A suppression as the API shows it. There is deliberately no hash field here.

email.description: Address scope only; null on an erasure tombstone, whose plaintext was destroyed.

lifted_at.description: Set when lifted. A lifted row stays, as history.

workspace_id.description: Null for an instance-wide suppression, which applies to every workspace.

UpdateContact.description:
A JSON Merge Patch (RFC 7386) of a contact: a field left out is left alone, and an explicit
`null` removes it. The address cannot change, so `email` is an unknown field here and is
rejected, not ignored.

attributes.description:
Merged into the stored attributes key by key: a key left out keeps its value. A key set to
`null` is removed, also for an archived field; any other value for an archived field is
refused. `attributes` itself cannot be `null`.

first_name.description: `null` clears it to an empty string.

last_name.description: `null` clears it to an empty string.

timezone.description: An IANA time zone such as `Europe/London`. `null` clears it.

UpdateCustomField.description:
`key` is immutable, so an unknown field (`key` included) is rejected, not ignored. `kind` is
accepted only so that a change can be refused with a message that says why.

oneOf.description: Must equal the field's current kind: changing it is not supported yet.

UpdateList.description: A field left out is left alone.

double_optin.description:
Only decides the status of members added from now on. A member already `pending` stays
`pending` (not mailable) when this is switched off.

UpdateWorkspace.description: The slug cannot change in M0, so an unknown field (`slug` included) is rejected, not ignored.

Visibility.description: Stored as text under a `check` constraint, not a Postgres enum.

Workspace.description: A workspace as one caller sees it: `role` is the caller's own.
